newsitem.title: INDIA: India edible oil prices to ease in late December.
newsitem.headline: India edible oil prices to ease in late December.

text.p: Indian edible oil prices are expected to dip by 500 rupees per tonne following optimum arrivals at the end of December, traders and industry officials said on Wednesday.

"Crop arrivals are quite good, but prices are expected to fall another 500 rupees when the arrivals reach the peak during end-December," O.P.Goenka, president of the Central Organisation of Oil Industry and Trade, told Reuters.
Traders said groundnut oil was currently quoted at around 36,000 rupees per tonne and palm olein was quoted at 27,000-27,200 rupees per tonne, the same as last week.
Last week industry officials said palm olein prices fell by around 500 rupees to 27,400 rupees per tonne during the week.
"The (edible oil domestic) market is quite stable," A.B. Godrej, director of Godrej Soaps and Godrej Foods, told Reuters.

Industry officials said the domestic demand for edible oil in 1996/97 (November-October) would be 300,000 tonnes more than last year's. India consumes over seven million tonnes of edible oil annually.
"The Indian crop is quite good. The extra demand this year will be met by the domestic crop itself," Godrej said.
According to trade estimates, the domestic production of oilseeds in 1996/97 is expected to be 21.5 million tonnes compared with 21 million last year.
Traders said edible oil imports had thinned down on better crop arrivals.
"Imports currently will be lower. Major imports will be from July to October," Godrej added.
